rules: Glob `ruststream_sea_file::file::prelude::*` on a stream file, `ruststream_sea_file::stdio::prelude::*` on a pipeline, and `ruststream_sea_file::prelude::*` in a service on both, writing `FilePublish` and `StdioPublish` (Components > Broker > Prelude).

Subscribe to a stream file with `#[subscriber(FileStream::new("key"))]`, the descriptor the AsyncAPI document describes; a bare `#[subscriber("key")]` is the stdio form (Components > Subscriptions > FileStream).
Open a subscription at a position with `start_at(FilePosition::beginning() | end() | sequence(n) | timestamp(millis))` (Components > Positions > start_at).
Read a finished file in one pass with `FileStream::new(key).replay()`, which completes at the end of the file or at the end-of-stream mark (Components > Subscriptions > replay).

Resume where a run stopped: store one past the sequence `Ctx<Position>` read last and open with `start_at(FilePosition::sequence(n))`, since `ack` and `nack` report `AckError::Unsupported` (Components > Positions > start_at).

Move a running file subscription from its handler with `Ctx<SeekHandle>`; it belongs to the file transport, and a handler that reads it does not compile against `StdioBroker` (Components > Positions > Seek).

Name the policy `Publish` at the mount site (`.out_reply(Publish)`, `.out(Marker, Publish)`); a handler body imports `ruststream::prelude::*` and bounds a slot as `Out<impl Publisher, Marker>` (Components > Publishing).

On a stream file a `retry_after` copy returns to the key its subscription reads; a stdio registration names the copy's key with `.out_retry(Publish).to("key")` (Components > Settlement > retry_after, out_retry).
Cap retries with `.max_attempts(n)` and `.dead_letter("key")` right after `include`; the count travels in the framework's retry-count header on every copy (Components > Settlement > Retries).

Take batches with a `&[T]` handler and `.batch(n)` at the mount site; the batch is assembled on the client and a partial one goes out 10 ms after its first delivery (Components > Subscriptions > Batches).
Test the production app with `TestApp::start` (feature `testing`), which connects `FileBroker` and `StdioBroker` in process, addressed as `tb.broker::<FileBroker>()` (Components > Testing).
Run the same test body against a real stream file with `TestApp::start_live` (Components > Testing > Live).
